summary: John's 7th-great-grandfather per the tree (if the Doll link holds); Palatine immigrant of 1739 to Plainfield Township - NOT a Revolutionary captain, despite the tree.
bio: Johann Casper Doll was baptized 1 Feb 1722 at Ulmet, Kusel district, son of Christoffel Doll (1671-1739) and Anna Sara Schuch (WikiTree Doll-527, FamilySearch N5BL-88G); his gravestone gives 2 Feb 1724 and the tree 1724-1793. WikiTree's API in Oct 2026 gave his birthplace as 'Oberland, Canton, Switzerland' (unsupported; Ulmet treated as probable). Round 3 corrected his arrival: 'Casper Doll, age 18' was on the ship Samuel (Hugh Percy), qualified at Philadelphia 27 Aug 1739 (Strassburger List 69 A; signature 'Caspar (X) Doll'), with Stoffel Doll 40, Philip Doll 27, 'Christ. Shook, 48' (Schuch) and Simon Drum - a group from Ulmet; the Samuel of 30 Aug 1737 (List 44), cited earlier, has no Casper. He married Anna Margaretha Dietz; a daughter Anna Catharine was baptized in 1757 at Tohickon Reformed Church, Bucks Co., to 'Casper Doll and Margaret [Dietz]'. He died 4 Feb 1793 and is buried at Plainfield Cemetery, Plainfield Twp (Wind Gap), Northampton Co. (Find a Grave 19353732). The tree calls him 'Johann C Doll Captain' with a 'FLAG OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION' profile image, but 'he is NOT known to have held the rank as captain. On his gravesite, there was erected in 1934 a monument or cenotaph to his nephew Casper Dull who served as a captain in the Revolutionary War'; that nephew, Capt. Casper Dull (1748-1829), is buried at McVeytown, Mifflin Co. His Find a Grave memorial merges the two. He was about 52 in 1776. No SAR patriot record for him was found (search not exhaustive); DAR unchecked.
